subject: Dedicated capacity playbook — technical deep-dive scheduling and prep
content:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah@nimbus.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity playbook — technical deep-dive scheduling and prep

Hi team / Sarah,

Following up on the pre-sales call last week — Nimbus requested a deep technical session that walks through our dedicated GPU capacity playbook: pool sizing, autoscaling behavior, tenant isolation options, and failure-mode runbooks. They want engineering-level detail rather than a product demo.

Proposed agenda (30–45m):
- 5m: goals and current constraints (Nimbus infra)
- 10m: capacity topology & autoscale patterns (reserved pools, burst)
- 10m: isolation and tenancy controls (network, KMS, audit trails)
- 10m: failure scenarios & runbook excerpt (cache warmup, preemption, fallbacks)
- 5m: next steps / draft POA

Proposed times (PST):
- Tue Mar 9 — 10:00–10:45
- Wed Mar 10 — 13:00–13:45
- Thu Mar 11 — 09:00–09:45

Ask: Marcus/Karthik/Mina — can each of you take a segment to cover? Marcus on topology & sizing, Karthik on autoscaling and routes, Mina on isolation & runbook. Also attaching a first-pass playbook PDF and our runbook notes to help prep.

Attachments:
- dedicated-playbook-v1.pdf (overview + diagrams)
- capacity-runbook-notes.docx (runbook excerpts)

Sarah / James — which of the above slots looks best for your engineering team? If none, propose two alternatives and timezone.

Thanks,
Soojin
--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0128

-----
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@nimbus.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Liao <james.liao@nimbus.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity playbook — technical deep-dive scheduling and prep

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear agenda.

Nimbus engineering prefers Wed Mar 10 at 13:00 PST. Our infra lead (James) will join, and we may bring one backend engineer (TBD). Main asks up front: confirm how long cache warmup takes for a 4x A100 pool at 2k seq, and what isolation surface looks like if we want hardware-tenant separation (we are evaluating VPC + dedicated pools).

Also, can you include whether Redwood supports encrypted KV-cache at rest? That will be an RFP item.

Sarah
Head of Platform / Nimbus AI

-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah@nimbus.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity playbook — technical deep-dive scheduling and prep

Wed 3/10 at 13:00 PST works for me. I'll take topology and sizing. Quick notes for prep:
- I'll bring a slide with our latency/throughput curves for 1/2/4-A100 pools at 512/1k/2k seq and expected per-token costs.
- Need Karthik to confirm autoscale buffer (we've been recommending 10–20% reserved for burst).
- Will include a failover diagram (multi-region fallback) if we have time.

Flagging one ask: do we want to show a short runbook snippet for a preemption event? Might be useful to show practical steps. Mina, you on runbook?

-Marcus
Senior Infrastructure PM | Redwood Inference

-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah@nimbus.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity playbook — technical deep-dive scheduling and prep

Confirmed for Wed 3/10 13:00 PST. I'll cover autoscale heuristics and smart routing (latency vs cost policy). A couple of prep notes:
- Autoscale buffer: we should present recommended defaults (5–15% for steady state, 20–30% for aggressive bursty workloads) and show cost trade-offs.
- For Nimbus's question on KV-cache encryption: short answer is yes (customer KMS + envelope encryption); I'll have the security callout.
- Mina: can you attach runbook excerpts showing the preemption play and the steps to warm a cache after failover? That will answer their warmup question more concretely.

Also adding a doc link to the internal playbook so we can pull numbers: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/DEMO-NIMBUS-3472

-Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime

-----
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Patel <sarah@nimbus.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity playbook — technical deep-dive scheduling and prep

Attached the runbook excerpt and a short appendix on cache-warm strategies. See attachments.

A couple of clarifications for the call:
- Cache warmup for a 4-A100 pool at 2k seq: realistic warm window to get KV hit rate to >80% is ~6–12 minutes depending on prefix reuse and batch size. We'll show a quick simulation slide.
- For hardware-tenant separation: we support dedicated pools + VPC peering; we do not recommend physical host pinning unless customer needs certified air-gapped hardware (we can discuss options).

I'll be on the call and can walk through the preemption play and the checklist for failover + cache rehydration.

Attachments:
- dedicated-playbook-v1.pdf
- capacity-runbook-notes.docx

Thanks,
Mina
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
